findings.title: Do not change notification preferences through an unprotected GET
findings.body: The new GET route immediately saves a notification-level change for the authenticated user, without a confirmation or recipient-specific token. Rails CSRF protection does not protect GET requests, so an attacker can send a logged-in user to a known topic's unsubscribe URL and silently downgrade or mute its notifications. Serve the confirmation page on GET and perform the change through a CSRF-protected request, or require an appropriately scoped signed token.

findings.title: Record the unsubscribe as an explicit notification preference change
findings.body: Saving the TopicUser directly bypasses TopicUser.change, which sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed and records notifications_changed_at. For records whose reason is nil, TopicUser.update_last_read can subsequently replace the unsubscribed regular or muted level with tracking once the reading threshold is reached. The unsubscribe therefore does not persist as an explicit user choice. Use the existing notification-change API rather than only assigning notification_level.

findings.title: Handle users without an existing TopicUser record
findings.body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil, but the next statement unconditionally calls notification_level on it. Although sending an email creates a record for its intended recipient, the URL contains no recipient identity and acts on current_user: opening a forwarded email, or opening it while signed into another account that has not visited the topic, produces a 500 response. Initialize the missing per-user topic state and apply the unsubscribe through TopicUser.change, which already supports creating records.

findings.title: Apply the unsubscribe when entering the route client-side
findings.body: This route only loads the ordinary topic view; it never invokes the unsubscribe action. Notification preferences are changed solely by the initial Rails GET to the unsubscribe URL. When the Ember application transitions to this route client-side, that GET is not made, yet the template tells the user they will stop receiving notifications. Ensure entering the client route performs the unsubscribe through a protected mutation request before displaying the success message.
